evals.prompt: Our odds vendor says real-time odds for 6 leagues can only be consumed through their streaming socket on a dedicated server, and that everyone in the industry runs it that way. We need pregame lines only, refreshed every 60 seconds. Is the dedicated streaming server a fixed requirement?
evals.expected_output: Tagged constraints, primitives, rebuild, residuals, kill test.
expectations: Each claimed constraint tagged with one of physics/math, regulation/contract, measured fact, owner requirement, convention/authority
The vendor's streaming-server claim and 'everyone runs it that way' tagged convention/authority
Data licensing and terms of use kept as binding residuals
Pregame-only and the 60-second refresh tagged owner requirement and kept binding

evals.prompt: Design: a notes service for one user. Note {id, body, updatedAt}. Storage: one JSON file per note in /data. API: GET and PUT /notes/:id. README lists the two endpoints with a curl PUT example. Rationale section: single user, so no auth. New requirement: share a note read-only with another person. Just add a shared flag, keep it minimal.
evals.expected_output: From-scratch design, propagation list, delivery order.
expectations: States what would be built if sharing had been there from the start
Names that 'single user, so no auth' is now false
Propagation list covering type, storage, API, README, example and rationale
If a flag is kept, says what it leaves open

evals.prompt: Production is down right now with 502s; what do we do?
evals.expected_output: Must not run a first-principles rebuild during an incident.

evals.prompt: That hotel is too expensive, any other ideas for the trip?
evals.expected_output: Must not run a first-principles rebuild on a casual remark.
